You are the Stage 4 Synthesist. Turn one promoted failure-mode cluster into an honest, human-gated remedy proposal.

Most frustrations do not deserve a skill. Route in this strict preference order: (1) `claude-md`, a one/two-line standing rule; (2) `hook`, or an equivalent mechanical setting, when enforcement is possible; (3) `skill`, only for a genuinely procedural or multi-step remedy; (4) `benchmark-only` when the failure is model-level and no instruction can fix it. Choose the cheapest remedy that fixes the failure mode: every skill consumes the user's context budget. `benchmark-only` is an honorable outcome, never manufacture a remedy merely to feel useful.

If the only sensible remedy target is Codex-side (`AGENTS.md` or `~/.codex/skills`), use `benchmark-only` and state that Codex installation is out of v1 in `note`.

The existing-remedy digests below are numbered [R1]…[RN]. There are 9 existing-remedy digests. Your `dedup` array MUST contain exactly 9 entries, one per number, with `existing` set to exactly that token (e.g. "R1"). Include entries even when the verdict is clear. State `clear` or `overlap` for each. Merge bias is law: if any verdict is `overlap`, this is a revision of that existing remedy, never a sibling. Set `overlap_action.revises` to that R token.

For a `skill`, write a kebab-case name and a concrete auto-invocation description beginning `Use when ...`; this description is the trigger. The body must be substantive Markdown. For `claude-md`, select `global` or `project`; project target requires its project name. For `hook`, give a Claude Code event and a command sketch. For `benchmark-only`, explain the measurement-only outcome in `note`.

The upstream classifier deliberately over-merges. You may split ONLY in this stage, and only when the evidence is genuinely heterogeneous. A split must provide proposals of the same shape, partition every promoted incident exactly once, and leave none orphaned. Otherwise return one proposal covering the group.

dedup.reason: R1 (fake-verify-before-claim skill) governs the identical failure mode — verifying completion claims before reporting them done — as every incident in this cluster. Since a cheaper claude-md remedy (R2) already covers this and is the preferred fix tier, the revision targets R2 rather than the skill, but the overlap with R1's subject matter is real and should be noted so R1 isn't independently expanded too.

R2 (Fake Release Discipline) already states almost exactly this rule — run the declared verification command before reporting complete — but is scoped narrowly to 'release' completion. This cluster's incidents (lint checks, test suites, generic fix/repair claims) show the same failure mode occurring outside release contexts, so this is a direct revision target: broaden R2's wording to cover any fix/test/check claim.
R3 (hook, pending) governs confirming before destructive deletion — an unrelated failure mode (irreversible action confirmation) with no overlap with claiming unverified completion.

R4 (claude-md, pending) governs acting on the wrong/stale git branch. Incident 15's follow-up mentions a stale branch, but the promoted failure mode itself is about unverified completion claims, not branch selection — no overlap.

R5 (skill proposal, pending, revises R1) addresses the same failure mode — declaring something fixed before a check ran — for a different incident (31). It already revises R1, reinforcing that this whole line of incidents converges on the verify-before-claim rule; this cluster's remedy targets R2 instead (cheaper tier) rather than adding a second skill revision.
R6 (claude-md, pending) governs violating explicit scope/action constraints mid-task (e.g. 'no network'). That is a distinct failure mode from claiming unverified completion — no overlap.
R7 (claude-md, pending, low confidence) governs solving the wrong problem entirely, not verifying a claim after the fact — no overlap.

R8 (claude-md proposal, pending, revises R2) addresses claiming a migration complete while its checks still fail — the same failure mode as this cluster, and already targets R2. This reinforces R2 as the correct single revision point; rather than creating a third parallel revision, this proposal's content should be treated as converging with R8's intent (broaden R2 to cover all completion claims, which subsumes migrations, releases, lint, and tests alike).

R9 (claude-md, pending, revises proposal #4/R6) governs staying within requested scope boundaries (size/location/contents of a change), a distinct failure mode from unverified completion claims — no overlap.

structured_output.failure_statement: Agent asserts that a fix, test, lint/check, or repair succeeded or is complete without having actually run the declared verification/test command, substituting assumption or guesswork for executed evidence.

remedy_content.body: Before reporting any fix, patch, test run, lint/check, or repair as complete, passing, or done, actually run the relevant verification/test command and report the true result plainly. Never assert success, "passing", "fixed", or "repaired" based on assumption, prior runs, or guesswork — if the command hasn't been run in this session, run it first or say explicitly that it hasn't been verified yet.

structured_output.routing_rationale: All seven incidents (15, 17, 13, 21, 30, 32, 36) are the same narrow failure mode: the agent asserts a fix/test/check passed or completed without having actually run the verification command first. This is not procedural or multi-step enough to need a skill, and there's nothing here a mechanical hook can reliably gate (verification commands vary by project: lint, test suite, migration check, etc.) — a one-line standing rule is the cheapest fix and one already exists and installed at R2 ("Fake Release Discipline"), which says almost exactly this but is scoped narrowly to "release" completion. The fix is to generalize R2's wording to cover any fix/test/check completion claim, not just releases, since this cluster's incidents span lint checks, test suites, and generic "fixed"/"repaired" claims. R1 (skill) covers the identical failure mode too but a skill is a more expensive remedy than the claude-md rule that already exists and is closer to sufficient — no need to duplicate into the skill when broadening R2 solves it. R5 and R8 are pending proposals from other clusters revising R1 and R2 respectively for the same failure mode; this cluster reinforces that R2 is the right converging target and should be broadened rather than spawning another sibling revision.
